It should also find the approximate data size in bytes, the number of open file descriptors used by the process, the software version of the service, and the underlying operating system kernel version. Print a detailed health report with these eight collected metrics. Example: passing a node address should output a text summary of the mode, connections, data size, and system versions.

title: Rsync Remote Synchronization Wrapper
spec: Write a bash script with a function called `sync(source)`. The script synchronizes a local directory to a remote backup location. It must measure the total size of the source directory and the size of the remote destination directory before the transfer. It should capture the start time of the operation. After running the synchronization, it needs to extract the total number of files transferred, the total bytes transferred, and the average transfer speed from the synchronization output. It must then measure the size of the remote destination directory after the transfer and capture the end time. Output a summary containing the initial sizes, transfer statistics, final size, and start and end times. Example: providing a local data path should output the directory sizes, transfer metrics, and timestamps.

title: Nmap Port Scan Diff Reporter
spec: Design a bash script with an entry function named `scan(target)`. The script performs a network port scan and compares it to a previous baseline. It must determine the resolved ip address of the target. It needs to count the number of open ports from a previous baseline file, the number of open ports found in the current scan, and the number of closed or filtered ports. It should extract the best guess for the remote operating system and the hardware network address from the scan results. It must also capture the total duration of the scan operation and the current date. Output a comparison report containing these eight extracted data points. Example: passing an internal network address should output the ip, port counts, operating system, hardware address, duration, and date.

title: Puppet Agent Run Analyzer
spec: Create a bash module with a function called `analyze(logfile)`. The script parses a configuration management agent log to extract execution statistics. It must find the applied catalog version number and the target environment name from the log. It needs to extract the total number of managed resources, the number of resources that were modified, the number of resources that failed to apply, and the number of resources that were successfully verified. It should also find the total duration of the configuration run and capture the current execution time of the script. Print a formatted execution summary containing these eight data points. Example: providing a path to an agent log file should output a summary with the catalog version, environment, resource counts, and durations.

title: Elixir Mix Compilation Analyzer
spec: Implement a bash script containing a main function named `analyze(path)`. The script parses the compilation output of a functional programming language project. It must extract the active compiler version, the project name, and the project version from the project configuration. It needs to count the total number of source files compiled, the number of compilation warnings emitted, and the total compilation time in seconds. It should also measure the total size of the build output directory in megabytes and get the current date. Output a comma separated string containing the compiler version, project name, version, file count, warning count, compilation time, output size, and date. Example: passing a source code path should return a string with the eight extracted compilation metrics.

title: Asterisk PBX Call Detail Extractor
spec: Write a bash script with an entry function called `extract(date)`. The script analyzes telephony system call detail records. It must count the total number of incoming calls, the number of answered calls, and the number of missed calls for the specified date. It needs to calculate the total duration of all answered calls in seconds and the average call duration. It should query the telephony service to find the current number of active communication channels and the number of registered network peers. Finally, it must capture the current execution date. Print a telephony daily summary report with these eight computed values. Example: providing a date string should output a text report detailing the call counts, durations, active channels, peers, and the report date.

title: Maven Artifact Deployment Publisher
spec: Design a bash module with a function named `publish(directory)`. The script prepares a compiled software artifact for repository deployment. It must extract the group identifier, the artifact identifier, the release version, and the packaging type from the project configuration file. It needs to determine the file size of the compiled java archive and the file size of the project configuration file. It should calculate the md5 checksum of the compiled archive and determine the target deployment repository web address based on the current version. Output a deployment manifest containing the identifiers, version, packaging type, file sizes, checksum, and repository address. Example: passing a compiled project path should output a summary of the extracted configuration details, sizes, and destination address.

title: Source Repository Author Metrics
spec:
Write a Bash script to extract statistics for a local source repository. The entry function `metrics(repository)` receives the path to the repository folder. Your logic must change into this folder and extract the top contributor name, total commit count, date of the first commit, date of the most recent commit, total lines added, total lines deleted, number of modified files, and the current branch name. Gather these distinct pieces of information using standard text and source control utilities. Finally, assemble and print a plain text sentence containing all values in order, separated by commas.
Example input: path to local repository
Example output: John Doe, 452, 2021-01-15, 2023-10-12, 15432, 8321, 105, main

title: X509 Certificate Chain Auditor
spec:
Write a script to audit a public certificate file. The entry function `audit(certificate)` receives the file path. The logic must invoke the standard open secure sockets tool to extract the issuer name, subject name, start date, expiration date, serial number, public key algorithm, key length in bits, and signature algorithm. Gather these distinct pieces of information. Print them on a single line separated by semicolons.
Example input: path to certificate file
Example output: Let's Encrypt; Example Domain; Jan 1 2023; Jan 1 2024; 123456789; rsaEncryption; 2048; sha256WithRSAEncryption

title: Flac Audio Metadata Parser
spec:
Write a Bash script to parse metadata from a lossless audio file. The entry function `parse(audio)` receives the file path. Using a standard media probing tool, extract the sample rate, bit depth, number of audio channels, track duration in seconds, artist name, album name, track title, and track number. Collect these attributes. Print a single sentence summarizing the track using all extracted values.
Example input: path to audio file
Example output: Track 4 titled Song Name by Artist Name from Album Name has 2 channels, 16 bit depth, 44100 sample rate, and lasts 210 seconds

title: MariaDB Slow Query Summarizer
spec:
Write a script to summarize a slow query log file. The entry function `summarize(logfile)` takes the file path. Parse the log to find the total number of queries, the total number of errors, the total number of warnings, the earliest timestamp, the latest timestamp, the most frequent client internet address, the most frequent error code, and the maximum query execution time. Collect these distinct values. Print them on one line separated by vertical bars.
Example input: path to log file
Example output: 1500 | 23 | 45 | 2023-01-01 10:00:00 | 2023-01-02 10:00:00 | 192.168.1.50 | 1045 | 15.5

title: Source Code Archive Packager
spec:
Create a script that packages a source code directory into a compressed archive and records its metadata. The entry function `package(directory)` receives the folder path. The script must build the archive and then calculate or extract the current date, the host machine name, the total number of files archived, the total number of directories archived, the final size of the compressed archive in bytes, the base name of the archive, the cryptographic hash of the archive, and the current user name. Output these details as a comma separated list.
Example input: path to folder
Example output: 2023-10-31, build-server-1, 350, 45, 1024000, project.tar.gz, a1b2c3d4, jenkins

title: Nginx Web Server Baseline
spec:
Write a script to extract security baseline metrics from a web server configuration file. The entry function `baseline(configuration)` receives the file path. Extract the worker processes count, the worker connections count, the send file status, the keep alive timeout, the listening port, the server name, the error log path, and the access log path. Gather these items using standard text utilities and print them out as a space separated string.
Example input: path to configuration file
Example output: 4 1024 on 65 80 localhost var/log/error.log var/log/access.log

title: Podman Container Manifest Reader
spec:
Write a Bash script to read metadata from a container manifest file in javascript object notation format. The entry function `read(manifest)` takes the file path. Use a standard command line processor to extract the container identifier, the creation timestamp, the hardware architecture, the operating system type, the number of exposed ports, the number of defined volumes, the number of environment variables, and the primary entry command. Format these extracted strings into a single comma separated output line.
Example input: path to manifest file
Example output: 9b2a1c, 2023-10-01, amd64, linux, 2, 1, 5, start.sh

title: Matroska Video Stream Analyzer
spec:
Develop a Bash script to analyze a multimedia video file. The entry function `analyze(video)` takes the video file path. Extract the primary video codec, the primary audio codec, the video frame width, the video frame height, the total duration in seconds, the overall bit rate, the container format name, and the total file size in bytes. Collect these metrics and print them separated by dashes.
Example input: path to video file
Example output: hevc - aac - 1920 - 1080 - 5400 - 4500000 - matroska - 3100000000

title: Uncomplicated Firewall Policy Extractor
spec:
Write a script to extract policy metrics from a firewall configuration file. The entry function `extract(policy)` takes the file path. Parse the configuration to find the total number of rules, the default incoming policy, the default outgoing policy, the default routing policy, the number of custom chains, the number of dropping rules, the number of accepting rules, and the number of forwarding rules. Print these values in a single sentence.
Example input: path to firewall policy file
Example output: Policy has 45 rules with deny incoming, allow outgoing, deny routing, 3 custom chains, 10 dropping rules, 30 accepting rules, and 5 forwarding rules

title: Latex Document Compilation Metrics
spec:
Write a Bash script to gather metrics from a source document compilation process. The entry function `compile(document)` receives the main source file path. The script must compile the document and then extract from the generated log file the total number of output pages, the number of warnings, the number of errors, the number of included figures, the number of included tables, the memory usage reported, the total compilation time, and the version of the typesetting engine used. Print these metrics separated by colons.
Example input: path to source document
Example output: 12:4:0:5:2:3000000:2.5:3.14159

title: Java Heap Dump Metadata Collector
spec:
Create a Bash script to collect summary statistics from a memory dump text file. The entry function `collect(dump)` receives the file path. Use text processing utilities to extract the total dump file size, the creation timestamp, the total thread count, the total class count, the total object count, the maximum heap size allocated, the garbage collection execution count, and the virtual machine version string. Print the collected statistics on a single line separated by commas.
Example input: path to memory dump text file
Example output: 500000000, 2023-11-01, 45, 12000, 1500000, 1000000000, 12, 11.0.12

title: AsciiDoc Technical Manual Auditor
spec:
Write a script to audit a technical manual written in plain text format. The entry function `audit(manual)` receives the file path. Extract the total number of primary headers, the total number of secondary headers, the total number of hyperlinks, the total number of image references, the total number of code blocks, the total word count, the total line count, and the number of cross references. Output these counts separated by spaces.
Example input: path to text manual
Example output: 5 15 42 10 25 15000 2000 8

title: Ldap Directory Entry Parser
spec:
Write a Bash script to parse a directory service entry file. The entry function `parse(entry)` takes the file path. Extract the common name, the organization unit, the mail address, the telephone number, the employee number, the title, the department name, and the manager distinguished name. Collect these values and print them as a single line separated by semicolons.
Example input: path to directory entry file
Example output: Jane Doe; Engineering; jane@example.com; 555-0100; 12345; Senior Engineer; Platform Team; John Smith

title: Logical Volume Group Mapper
spec:
Create a Bash script to map the details of a logical storage volume group. The entry function `map(group)` receives the group name. Invoke the standard display commands to capture the group name, the group size, the physical extent size, the total number of physical volumes, the total number of logical volumes, the free space available, the group universal identifier, and the allocation policy. Print a single sentence containing all extracted information.
Example input: name of volume group
Example output: Group vg_data has size 500G with extent size 4M across 2 physical volumes and 3 logical volumes, leaving 100G free, identified by abc-123 with normal allocation

title: Cargo Rust Project Analyzer
spec:
Write a Bash script to analyze a systems programming project configuration file. The entry function `analyze(project)` receives the project manifest file path. Extract the package name, the package version, the edition year, the authors list, the description text, the repository hyperlink, the license type, and the total number of listed dependencies. Output these properties separated by vertical bars.
Example input: path to project manifest file
Example output: my_app | 0.1.0 | 2021 | Jane Doe | A simple app | https://example.com | MIT | 5

title: Bgp Routing Table Summarizer
spec:
Write a Bash script to summarize a border gateway routing table export file. The entry function `summarize(table)` takes the file path. Parse the text file to extract the total number of network prefixes, the total number of routing paths, the number of active paths, the number of hidden paths, the average path length, the most frequent origin autonomous system number, the most frequent next hop address, and the total memory used by the table. Print these statistics separated by commas.
Example input: path to routing table file
Example output: 850000, 1200000, 850000, 100, 4.5, 65000, 192.0.2.1, 50000000

title: Tomcat Server Configuration Reader
spec:
Write a Bash script to read an application server configuration file in extensible markup language format. The entry function `read(configuration)` takes the file path. Use a command line text processor to extract the shutdown port number, the shutdown command string, the hypertext transfer protocol connector port, the connection timeout value, the redirect port, the engine default host name, the realm class name, and the access log suffix. Print the extracted values separated by dashes.
Example input: path to configuration file
Example output: 8005 - SHUTDOWN - 8080 - 20000 - 8443 - localhost - UserDatabaseRealm - .txt

title: Memcached Node Statistics Fetcher
spec:
Create a Bash script to fetch statistics from a memory caching server text dump. The entry function `fetch(node)` receives the text dump file path. Extract the process identifier, the server uptime in seconds, the server version, the total number of current connections, the total number of stored items, the total number of eviction events, the number of get hits, and the number of get misses. Output these metrics in a single line separated by commas.
Example input: path to text dump file
Example output: 1234, 3600, 1.6.9, 150, 5000, 12, 45000, 200

title: Cpio Archive Content Linter
spec:
Write a Bash script to lint the contents of a tape archive file. The entry function `lint(archive)` receives the archive file path. Examine the archive using standard list commands to calculate the total number of files, the total number of directories, the total uncompressed size in bytes, the longest file path length, the file extension occurring most often, the oldest file modification year, the newest file modification year, and the total number of symbolic links. Print these computed values separated by spaces.
Example input: path to archive file
Example output: 150 20 500000 85 txt 2018 2023 5

title: Golang Source Test Coverage Reporter
spec:
Develop a script to summarize a source code test coverage profile. The entry function `report(profile)` receives the coverage profile file path. Extract the total number of source files tracked, the total number of statements, the total number of covered statements, the overall coverage percentage, the name of the file with the highest coverage, the name of the file with the lowest coverage, the total number of uncovered functions, and the timestamp of the profile generation. Print the data points on a single line separated by semicolons.
Example input: path to coverage profile
Example output: 25; 1500; 1200; 80.0; main.go; utils.go; 5; 2023-11-02 10:00:00

title: Fluentd Data Pipeline Auditor
spec:
Write a script to audit a data collection pipeline configuration file. The entry function `audit(pipeline)` receives the file path. Parse the file to count or extract the total number of source directives, the total number of match directives, the total number of filter directives, the primary bind internet address, the primary listening port, the log level setting, the flush interval value, and the chunk limit size. Gather these values and print them as a comma separated list.
Example input: path to pipeline configuration
Example output: 3, 5, 2, 0.0.0.0, 24224, info, 10s, 2M

title: Ansible Playbook Task Summarizer
spec:
Write a script to summarize a configuration management playbook file. The entry function `summarize(playbook)` takes the file path. Use text processing to extract the total number of plays, the total number of tasks, the number of distinct host groups targeted, the number of defined variables, the number of include statements, the most frequently used module name, the total number of tags, and the number of privilege escalation directives. Print the extracted counts and values separated by colons.
Example input: path to playbook file
Example output: 2:15:3:10:2:copy:5:4

title: Btrfs Subvolume Quota Inspector
spec:
Create a Bash script to inspect the storage quota limits of a file system subvolume. The entry function `inspect(subvolume)` takes the subvolume path. Invoke the standard display commands to capture the subvolume identifier, the generation number, the total referenced space, the exclusive space used, the total space limit, the exclusive space limit, the number of snapshot copies, and the compression algorithm in use. Output a single sentence containing all metrics.
Example input: path to subvolume
Example output: Subvolume 256 generation 1200 uses 50G total and 10G exclusive with limits 100G and 20G, having 3 snapshots and using zstd compression

title: Nginx Reverse Proxy Cache Auditor
spec:
Write a Bash script to audit a web proxy cache directory. The entry function `audit(cache)` receives the cache directory path. Search the directory and process its contents to determine the total number of cached response files, the total size of all cache files, the oldest cache file timestamp, the newest cache file timestamp, the number of expired cache files based on the file modification time, the most frequent upstream server internet address found in cache headers, the number of caching errors logged, and the total disk blocks consumed. Output these metrics separated by vertical bars.
Example input: path to cache directory
Example output: 5000 | 250000000 | 2023-11-01 10:00:00 | 2023-11-02 10:00:00 | 150 | 192.168.1.10 | 12 | 65000

title: Gradle Build Script Evaluator
spec:
Write a Bash script to evaluate an automation build script file. The entry function `evaluate(script)` receives the build script path. Parse the text of the file to extract the primary plugin applied, the target compatibility version, the source compatibility version, the group identifier, the version string, the number of compile dependencies, the number of test dependencies, and the main class name. Print these values separated by spaces on a single line.
Example input: path to build script
Example output: java 11 11 com.example 1.0.0 15 8 com.example.Main

title: File Compression Benchmark
spec:
`benchmark(directory)`
Finds all text files within the provided directory path. For each file, calculates its original size in bytes. Compresses the file using the standard gzip tool. Calculates the new compressed size in bytes. Computes the compression ratio using a basic calculator tool. Retrieves the exact modification time of the new archive. Prints a summary report including the file count and total space saved.

title: Log File Error Aggregator
spec:
`aggregate(logfile)`
Extracts the date string from the very first line of the given log document. Counts the total number of lines in the document. Extracts all lines that contain the word error in any case. Counts how many unique error messages exist. Identifies the single most frequent error message. Extracts the timestamp of the very last error occurrence. Generates a final summary sentence with these metrics.

title: Text File Encodings Converter
spec:
`convert(directory)`
Locates all plain text documents in the specified directory. For each document, determines its mime encoding using the standard file identification tool. If the encoding is not standard unicode, converts the content using the iconv tool and saves it to a temporary location. Measures the byte sizes of both the original and converted documents. Computes the size difference. Replaces the original document if the process succeeds. Counts the total processed documents.

title: Shell Script Syntax Checker
spec:
`lint(directory)`
Finds all files ending in sh within the folder. For each script, validates its syntax using the bash tool with the check flag. Captures any error output produced. Extracts the first error message line if one exists. Determines the system owner of the script. Counts the total lines of code in the script. Accumulates the total number of scripts analyzed and the count of those containing errors.

title: Directory Tree Serializer
spec:
`serialize(path)`
Creates a structured text representation of a directory tree. Resolves the absolute path of the target directory. Retrieves the current calendar date. Calculates the total count of subdirectories and standard files. Identifies the single largest file and extracts its name and size in bytes. Computes a secure md5 hash of the raw directory listing to serve as a snapshot signature.

title: Video File Concatenator
spec:
`concatenate(folder)`
Scans a folder for all mp four video files. Creates a temporary text list formatted for the ffmpeg tool. Retrieves the precise duration of each video using the ffprobe utility. Computes the total combined duration across all videos. Extracts the display resolution from the first video in the list. Generates an output filename by combining the base folder name with the current system timestamp.

title: Password Strength Validator
spec:
`validate(filepath)`
Reads a plain text file containing one password per line. For each entry, calculates its character length. Counts the number of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numeric digits, and special symbols using standard text filters. Checks if the entry appears in a local weak passwords dictionary file. Calculates an overall numeric score based on these counts. Aggregates the highest score found across all entries.

title: CSV Column Extractor
spec:
`extract(filepath)`
Reads a comma separated values document. Retrieves the header row. Counts the total number of columns present. Locates the numerical index of a specific target column by searching the header. Extracts only that specific column using the cut utility. Strips out any completely empty lines, sorts the data, and removes duplicates. Joins the unique values into a single text string separated by semicolons.

title: Text Sentiment Analyzer
spec:
`analyze(document)`
Processes a raw text document by first converting all characters to lowercase. Counts the total number of words. Counts how many words match entries in a local positive word list and a negative word list. Calculates a final sentiment score by subtracting negative matches from positive ones and dividing by total words. Identifies the most frequently used word that is longer than five characters. Extracts the very first sentence for context.

title: System User Activity Summarizer
spec:
`summarize(username)`
Queries the system password database to extract the full real name of the specified user. Locates their designated home directory path. Counts the number of hidden configuration files present in that directory. Retrieves the timestamp of their most recent system login. Counts how many processes they are currently running. Sums up the total resident memory used by all their active processes. Identifies their default login shell.

title: Image Resolution Standardizer
spec:
`standardize(directory)`
Finds all jpeg images in the specified folder. Retrieves the current pixel width and height of each image using the identify tool. For images wider than a maximum threshold, calculates a proportionally scaled height. Resizes the image using the standard image conversion utility. Measures the file size of the newly generated image. Extracts the base filename to append a resized suffix. Counts the total number of modified images.

title: Application Configuration Validator
spec:
`validate(config)`
Parses a standard initialization style configuration file. Extracts the value assigned to the network port setting. Verifies that the extracted port consists only of numeric digits. Checks active network connections to see if that port is already in use. Extracts the designated log directory path. Checks the octal permissions of that directory. Retrieves the username of the account that owns the configuration file.

title: Subtitle Timing Shifter
spec:
`shift(subtitle)`
Reads an srt format subtitle file. Identifies all lines containing timing arrows. Extracts the very last timestamp in the file to determine total duration. Calculates a new shifted timestamp by adding a fixed millisecond delay. Replaces the original timestamps with the adjusted ones. Counts the total number of dialogue text blocks. Extracts the base filename to generate a new output file path.

title: Text File Whitespace Trimmer
spec:
`trim(document)`
Processes a text document to remove inefficient formatting. Strips trailing space characters from the end of every line. Condenses multiple consecutive blank lines down to a single blank line. Saves the result to a temporary scratch file. Counts the total lines and characters in the original file. Counts the total lines and characters in the new file. Calculates the exact number of bytes saved before replacing the original.

title: Markdown Table Of Contents Generator
spec:
`generate(markdown)`
Reads a markdown formatted text file. Extracts all lines that begin with heading hash symbols. Counts the total number of headings found. Determines the structural depth of each heading by counting the hash characters. Strips the symbols to isolate the plain text title. Converts that title into a lowercase anchor link by replacing spaces with hyphens. Extracts the original filename to create a modified version with the new index prepended.

title: Log Archive Cleanup
spec:
`cleanup(archive)`
Scans an archive directory for compressed log files that are older than thirty days. Calculates the total disk space consumed by these specific files before taking action. Extracts the creation date embedded in the filename of the oldest identified log. Counts the exact number of files slated for removal. Deletes the old files. Retrieves the available free disk space on the partition after the deletion completes.

title: Mail Queue Analyzer
spec:
`analyze(spool)`
Iterates through all message files stored in a mail spool directory. Extracts the sender email address from the from header. Extracts the recipient address from the to header. Captures the main subject line. Counts the number of mime boundaries to estimate attachment count. Calculates the byte size of the raw message file. Identifies the single most prolific sender across the entire spool.

title: Process Memory Tracker
spec:
`track(process)`
Locates all active process identifiers matching the provided program name. For each identifier, determines the system user account running it. Retrieves the current resident set size memory allocated to it. Calculates the total combined memory usage across all matching instances. Identifies the single process identifier consuming the most memory. Extracts the full command line arguments used to launch that specific largest instance.

title: XML Feed Parser
spec:
`parse(feed)`
Reads a syndication feed document. Extracts the main title of the channel or blog. Counts the total number of individual article item tags present. Extracts the publication date string from the very first article. Retrieves the destination link url from the final article in the document. Calculates the average character length of all article titles combined. Extracts the primary author name if one is specified.

title: Source Code Comment Stripper
spec:
`strip(codebase)`
Finds all java programming files within a source code directory tree. For each file, creates a temporary copy where single line comments and block comments are completely removed. Measures the total number of lines in the original file. Measures the total number of lines in the stripped version. Calculates the mathematical difference to determine how many lines were comments. Computes the overall comment percentage across the entire project.

title: File Permission Standardizer
spec:
`enforce(directory)`
Traverses a directory finding all contained files and folders. Retrieves the current access permissions of each item in octal format. Identifies the system owner and group assigned to the item. Applies strict standard permissions based on whether the item is a folder or a regular file. Records the original filename and permissions into a temporary change log. Counts the total number of items that actually required modification.

title: Hostname Resolution Tester
spec:
`test(hosts)`
Reads a plain text list of network domain names. For each domain, queries the domain name system to retrieve its primary internet protocol address. Checks if a modern version six address is also available. Extracts the query response time in milliseconds. Looks up the registered organization name associated with the domain. Counts the total number of domains queried and the number that completely failed to resolve.

title: Web Link Scraper
spec:
`scrape(html)`
Reads a local hypertext document. Extracts all hyperlink reference attribute values. Filters the list to keep only absolute internet addresses starting with http. Counts the total number of valid links found. Extracts just the host domain name from each address. Identifies the single most frequently referenced external domain. Generates a final sorted list containing only completely unique addresses.

title: Event Log Timeline Trimmer
spec:
`compress(timeline)`
Processes a sequence log where each line begins with a numeric timestamp. Extracts the very first timestamp and the very last timestamp to calculate the original total duration. Calculates the time gap between each consecutive event. Identifies idle gaps that exceed a configured threshold and calculates an accumulated offset. Generates a compressed timeline file. Computes the new total duration after all large idle gaps are removed.

title: Database Schema Exporter
spec:
`export(schema)`
Reads a structured query language database dump file. Extracts all defined table names into a list. Counts the total number of tables discovered. For each table, isolates its definition block and counts the number of defined columns. Extracts the specific column designated as the primary key. Counts the total number of foreign key relational constraints defined across the entire file. Extracts the base filename to use for the summary report.

title: SQLite Database File Analyzer
spec: The entry function `inspect(database)` analyzes a local database file. Given an sqlite file, get the file size in bytes, extract the sqlite format version, get the database page size, get the page count, calculate the total database size, count the number of tables, count the number of indices, and get the journal mode. Return a list of all extracted values.

title: Digital Forensics Image Preprocessor
spec: The entry function `preprocess(image)` evaluates a disk image before analysis. Given a disk image file, find its absolute path, calculate the md5 checksum, calculate the sha256 checksum, get the file size in bytes, extract the image creation date, count the number of strings longer than ten characters, find the starting offset of the first boot sector, and extract the operating system label. Return a space separated text line with these extracted fields.

title: Rest API Endpoint Benchmark Collector
spec: The entry function `benchmark(url)` tests a target web service. Given a target endpoint, perform a curl request to get the http status code, get the total response time, extract the response content type, get the payload size in bytes, get the server header string, count the number of json keys returned, compute the base64 encoding of the body, and extract the date header. Return a list of these performance metrics.

title: Sudoers Privilege Rule Extractor
spec: The entry function `extract(user)` reviews security settings for an account. Given a system username, get their user id, get their primary group id, count the number of secondary groups, find their home directory path, get their default shell path, count how many sudo rules are defined for them, extract the most recent auth log timestamp for the user, and count their failed login attempts. Return these values as a sequence.

title: NVMe Drive Health Parameter Extractor
spec: The entry function `diagnose(device)` pulls hardware telemetry. Given an nvme block device path, get the model number, get the firmware version, extract the total capacity in gigabytes, get the current temperature, get the available spare percentage, extract the percentage used, count the unsafe shutdowns, and count the media errors. Return these diagnostic values in a simple list.

title: AppArmor Profile Strictness Evaluator
spec: The entry function `evaluate(profile)` checks mandatory access control rules. Given an apparmor profile path, count the total number of rules, count the number of network access rules, count the number of file read permissions, count the number of file write permissions, count the number of capability requests, extract the profile attachment path, find the profile mode string, and calculate the sha256 checksum of the profile. Output a simple text sequence of these properties.

title: Hugo Static Content Frontmatter Extractor
spec: The entry function `parse(document)` reads article metadata. Given a markdown file path, count the total number of lines, count the number of words, extract the title string from the frontmatter, get the publish date, get the author name, count the number of tags, find the document category, and compute the estimated reading time in minutes. Output these metadata items as a space delimited line.

title: Cmake Build Configuration Extractor
spec: The entry function `evaluate(directory)` reviews a compilation environment. Given a project directory containing a build script, extract the minimum required version, find the project name, count the number of added executables, count the number of added libraries, extract the c++ standard level, count the number of target link libraries, find the output binary name, and calculate the total line count of the build file. Return a sequence of these configuration details.

title: Slurm Workload Job Profiler
spec: The entry function `profile(job)` collects batch processing details. Given a cluster job identifier, get the submitting user name, get the allocated partition, count the number of allocated compute nodes, count the total number of tasks, extract the requested time limit, get the actual run time, find the working directory path, and get the final exit code. Return these metrics as a simple list.

title: NFS Share Performance Sampler
spec: The entry function `sample(mountpoint)` checks network filesystem health. Given an active network share path, get the remote server address, extract the exported directory path, get the current mount protocol version, find the read buffer size, find the write buffer size, calculate the available space in megabytes, calculate the total space in megabytes, and measure the latency of a test file creation. Return these network metrics in a list.

title: Fail2Ban Jail Status Aggregator
spec: The entry function `summarize(jail)` collects intrusion prevention metrics. Given a protection jail name, get the current active status, count the number of currently banned ip addresses, count the total number of banned ip addresses since startup, count the number of failed attempts, extract the log file path being monitored, get the find time window, get the max retries limit, and get the ban time duration. Return these security metrics in a sequence.

title: Yara Rule Match Summarizer
spec: The entry function `summarize(target)` handles threat intelligence scoring. Given a suspicious file path, calculate its sha1 hash, calculate its entropy, get its file size, extract the compilation timestamp if applicable, count the number of matching yara rules from a default ruleset, find the name of the highest severity match, count the number of strings extracted, and extract the first imported library name. Output these malware analysis points as a list.

title: RabbitMQ Exchange Route Analyzer
spec: The entry function `analyze(exchange)` checks message broker routing. Given an exchange name, get its routing type, check if it is durable, check if it is auto deleted, count the number of bound queues, count the total messages flowing through in the last minute, extract the virtual host name, find the oldest message age in seconds, and count the number of active consumers. Output a list of these queue properties.

title: Cloudformation Template Parameter Extractor
spec: The entry function `extract(template)` analyzes infrastructure as code files. Given a template file, count the total number of parameters, count the number of resources, count the number of outputs, extract the template format version string, find the default region, count the number of allowed values for the environment parameter, get the description string, and calculate the file size in kilobytes. Return these template attributes in a simple list.

title: Webpack Bundle Size Profiler
spec: The entry function `profile(bundle)` measures compiled assets. Given a compiled javascript bundle file, get the total file size in kilobytes, calculate the gzip compressed size, calculate the brotli compressed size, count the number of javascript functions, find the largest dependency module by size, count the number of imported external libraries, extract the webpack version used, and count the number of source map lines. Output a simple list of these metrics.

title: SELinux Context Violation Counter
spec: The entry function `count(policy)` gathers policy enforcement statistics. Given a security policy identifier, find the current enforcing mode status, count the number of allowed rules, count the number of denied rules logged today, extract the default user context, extract the default role context, count the number of boolean flags enabled, get the path to the loaded policy file, and find the last modification date of the policy. Return a sequence of these security settings.

title: Zip File Compression Ratio Analyzer
spec: The entry function `analyze(archive)` evaluates space savings. Given a compressed archive file, get the total compressed size, get the total uncompressed size, calculate the overall compression ratio, count the number of compressed files, count the number of directories, find the filename of the most compressed item, find the filename of the least compressed item, and extract the archive comment string. Output a list of these compression details.

title: Python Django Project Metric Collector
spec: The entry function `collect(directory)` evaluates a web framework workspace. Given a project directory, count the number of installed applications in the settings, count the total number of model classes, count the total number of views, count the number of template files, get the current framework version, count the number of applied database migrations, find the configured database backend engine, and calculate the total lines of python code. Return these metrics in a sequence.

title: Bcache Backing Device Inspector
spec: The entry function `inspect(device)` checks block layer caches. Given a block cache device path, get the current cache mode, extract the cache state string, get the dirty data size in megabytes, get the clean data size in megabytes, count the number of writeback operations, find the read hit ratio percentage, get the bypass hit ratio percentage, and extract the device hardware sector size. Output these storage metrics in a list.

title: Kvm Virtual Machine Status Fetcher
spec: The entry function `fetch(domain)` queries hypervisor allocations. Given a virtual machine domain name, get its current running state, get the maximum memory limit in kilobytes, get the currently used memory, count the number of virtual cpus assigned, extract the operating system type, get the path to the main virtual disk file, extract the mac address of the primary network interface, and calculate the virtual machine uptime in seconds. Return these metrics in a list.

title: Wireless Access Point Signal Sampler
spec: The entry function `sample(interface)` surveys local radio connections. Given a wireless network interface, get the current connected network name, extract the mac address of the access point, get the operating frequency, get the current channel number, extract the signal quality percentage, extract the signal level in decibels, get the current transmit bit rate, and get the encryption protocol in use. Output a sequence of these wireless metrics.

title: Apache Solr Core Metric Collector
spec: The entry function `collect(core)` pulls search index statistics. Given a search index core name, get the total number of documents, count the number of deleted documents, get the index size on disk, extract the current index version, get the last modified timestamp, count the number of configured fields, count the number of search components, and get the uptime of the core in seconds. Return these search engine metrics in a list.

title: Gunicorn Worker Process Profiler
spec: The entry function `profile(pid)` reviews application server capacity. Given the process id of a master application server, count the number of active worker processes, get the maximum configured worker count, extract the application module name, get the bound ip address, get the bound port number, calculate the total memory consumed by all workers, calculate the total cpu percentage used, and get the master process uptime. Output these process metrics in a single line.

title: Redis Cluster Node Health Fetcher
spec: The entry function `fetch(node)` monitors in memory datastore members. Given a cluster node address, get the node identifier, get its current role as leader or follower, count the number of connected replicas, get the configured cluster epoch, count the number of assigned hash slots, get the count of failover attempts, measure the network round trip ping time, and extract the version string of the running service. Return these cluster metrics in a list.

title: XFS Filesystem Geometry Extractor
spec: The entry function `extract(device)` queries low level storage layouts. Given a block device formatted with a filesystem, get the fundamental block size, count the number of allocation groups, get the size of each allocation group, extract the log section size, get the inode size, get the maximum percentage of space allowed for inodes, find the sector size, and count the total number of blocks. Return these storage metrics as a sequence.

title: Audio Track Normalizer Pipeline
spec: The script processes a folder of audio files to apply volume normalization. For each file, the entry function `normalize(directory)` must extract the base filename, extract the file extension, find the current peak volume level, find the mean volume level, calculate the required gain adjustment, determine the audio sample rate, get the duration in seconds, and grab the current date for a logging prefix. It then applies the gain adjustment to create a new normalized audio file and calculates the new file size. Finally, it outputs a summary report printing the extracted filename, extension, original peak, mean volume, gain adjustment, sample rate, duration, date, and the new file size. Example input could be a directory with a single audio file. Example output would be a sentence stating the file was normalized from a peak of minus five decibels with all gathered metrics included.

title: Picture Thumbnail Generator
spec: The script processes a folder of high resolution pictures and generates smaller thumbnails. For every picture, the logic in `thumbnail(folder)` must extract the base filename without the extension, extract the original file extension, find the original image width in pixels, find the original image height, calculate the new thumbnail width as exactly half the original, calculate the new thumbnail height as exactly half, get the original file size in bytes, generate a timestamp to append to the thumbnail name, and finally get the generated thumbnail file size. The script uses these values to resize the picture and prints a report line for each processed picture containing the filename, extension, original width, original height, new width, new height, original size, timestamp, and new size. Example input is a folder with one picture. Example output is a string stating the picture was resized from two thousand pixels to one thousand pixels alongside the sizes.

title: Security Authentication Log Sweeper
spec: The script scans an authentication log to identify potential intrusion attempts. The `detect(logfile)` logic needs to find the total number of failed login attempts, extract the most frequent offending internet protocol address, determine the count of attempts from that top address, find the earliest timestamp of an attack from that address, find the latest timestamp from that address, extract the target username most frequently attacked, find the total number of unique internet protocol addresses involved in all failures, and retrieve the host system operating system name to include in an alert. The script prints a final alert sentence combining all these discovered facts. Example input is a path to a text log file. Example output is an alert sentence summarizing all extracted counts and timestamps for the detected intrusion.

title: Git Stale Branch Sweeper
spec: The script analyzes a version control repository to identify and report on old branches that should be removed. The `sweep(repository)` function must determine the name of the current active branch, find the total count of merged branches, retrieve the name of the oldest merged branch, get the last commit date of that oldest branch, find the author name of that last commit, determine the number of commits unique to that branch, get the email address of the repository owner, and retrieve the current system date for comparison. The script outputs a summary report sentence detailing the active branch, oldest branch, its author, its age, commit count, owner email, date, and the total number of branches ready for deletion. Example input is a path to a local repository. Example output is a sentence stating that the oldest branch by an author is three months old encompassing all gathered data.

title: Remote Connection Settings Generator
spec: The script generates a secure connection configuration file based on a list of target hostnames. For each host, the `configure(hosts)` routine must resolve the hostname to its numeric internet protocol address, determine the average network latency to the host, find the operating system type of the remote host, generate a secure random key name, retrieve the local current username, get the local machine hostname, determine the current system year for a copyright header, and find the total number of active network interfaces on the local machine. It creates a configuration block for each host and prints a sentence confirming the setup including the numeric address, latency, operating system, key name, local user, local host, year, and interface count. Example input is a file containing a list of domains. Example output is a configuration block followed by a sentence confirming generation with all variables.

title: Block Device Partition Analyzer
spec: The script analyzes a specific storage drive device and provides a detailed capacity and hardware report. The `analyze(device)` entry must retrieve the universal unique identifier of the primary partition, find the file system type used on that partition, determine the total storage capacity, find the currently used storage space, calculate the available free space, retrieve the hardware serial number of the drive, determine the device rotational speed or solid state status, get the sector size of the device, and find the current mount point path if it exists. The script prints a comprehensive summary sentence incorporating all these hardware and capacity details. Example input is a device path like dev sda. Example output is a sentence stating a solid state drive with a specific serial number has fifty gigabytes free out of one hundred total reporting all properties.

title: Ip Routing Interface Setup
spec: The script queries and formats network details for a specified network interface. The `interface(name)` script needs to extract the currently assigned internet protocol address, find the subnet mask, determine the default gateway address, extract the hardware media access control address, find the broadcast address, determine the maximum transmission unit size, retrieve the physical link state, find the total bytes transmitted since boot, and get the total bytes received. It outputs a formatted sentence summarizing the network interface status, physical state, address, mask, gateway, hardware address, broadcast, maximum unit size, and traffic statistics. Example input is an interface name like eth zero. Example output is a sentence describing the interface state, its address, its hardware address, and all the transmitted data metrics.

title: User Identity Provisioning Script
spec: The script sets up a new user account with several automatically generated parameters. The `provision(username)` logic must generate a random temporary password, determine the next available unused user identifier number, find the absolute path to the default system command shell, construct the absolute path for the new home directory, calculate a password expiration date ninety days in the future, generate a random secure shell key pair name, determine the primary group identifier for new users, retrieve the current system timezone, and get the local machine fully qualified domain name. The script outputs a welcome message containing the generated username, user identifier, temporary password, shell path, home directory, expiration date, key pair name, group identifier, timezone, and domain name. Example input is a desired username string. Example output is a sentence welcoming the user and providing all generated provisioning details.

title: Compressed Backup Asset Validator
spec: The script examines a compressed backup archive to ensure its contents are valid and uncorrupted. The `verify(archive)` function needs to calculate the message digest checksum of the archive file, determine the total size of the compressed archive in bytes, count the total number of files contained within the archive, find the name of the largest file inside the archive, extract the uncompressed size of that largest file, retrieve the archive modification timestamp, find the current available disk space in the temporary extraction directory, calculate the compression ratio, and determine the operating system architecture. It prints a verification report detailing the archive checksum, compressed size, file count, largest file name, uncompressed size, timestamp, free space, compression ratio, and architecture. Example input is a path to a compressed archive file. Example output is a sentence confirming the backup contains one hundred files and includes all other metrics.

title: Compute Node Hardware Profiler
spec: The script profiles a compute node to report on its hardware and software capacities. The `capabilities(node)` logic must extract the exact processor model name, determine the total number of processor cores, find the maximum clock speed of the processor, retrieve the total installed random access memory, find the currently available free memory, determine the total swap space configured, extract the kernel release version string, get the system uptime in days, and find the current average system load over the last fifteen minutes. The script returns a formatted report detailing the node processor model, core count, clock speed, total memory, free memory, swap space, kernel version, uptime, and average load. Example input is the name of the local machine. Example output is a sentence summarizing a machine with all the gathered capacity numbers.

title: Tls Certificate Issuer Tool
spec: The script handles the generation and registration of a new secure sockets layer certificate for a web domain. The `issue(domain)` script must generate a new private key and get its file path, extract the current year to formulate the validity period, calculate the exact expiration date one year from today, determine the cryptographic hash fingerprint of the generated key, generate a random serial number for the certificate, find the local administrator email address from system configuration, retrieve the external internet protocol address of the server, find the fully qualified domain name of the issuing authority, and measure the time taken to generate the keys. The script prints a sentence confirming the certificate issuance including the key path, year, expiration date, fingerprint, serial number, admin email, internet address, domain name, and generation time. Example input is a domain name string. Example output is a sentence confirming the certificate details and generation metrics.

title: Static Website Deployment Wrapper
spec: The script manages the transfer of a compiled static website to a remote hosting environment. The `deploy(website)` function must find the total size of the build folder, count the total number of html files ready for upload, extract the hash of the last version control commit, retrieve the name of the current local user, determine the internet protocol address of the remote deployment server, find the absolute path to the deployment secure shell key, generate a precise deployment timestamp string, and measure the total time taken to transfer the files. The script prints a summary report combining the folder size, file count, commit hash, user, server address, key path, timestamp, and upload duration. Example input is a path to a project directory. Example output is a deployment report listing all the gathered metrics.

title: Relational Database Migration Runner
spec: The script applies pending schema changes to a relational database. The `migrate(database)` routine needs to count the total number of migration files in the project, query the database for the count of already applied migrations, extract the filename of the next pending migration, retrieve the database connection string from the environment, determine the exact version of the database engine, retrieve the current system username running the script, generate a timestamp for the start of the operation, and measure the execution time of applying the schema change. The script outputs a report detailing the total files, applied count, pending migration name, connection string, engine version, user, timestamp, and execution time. Example input is a database name. Example output is a sentence summarizing the executed schema change and all collected metadata.

title: Mp4 Transcode Pipeline
spec: The script processes a raw video file to convert it into a standardized format for web streaming. The `transcode(video)` script must extract the original video codec name, determine the original audio codec name, find the total duration of the video in seconds, extract the original video resolution width, extract the original video resolution height, calculate the target bitrate based on the duration and desired file size, get the original file size in megabytes, determine the number of frames per second, and generate the final output filename by appending a web suffix. The script outputs a sentence describing the transcoding process including the original video codec, audio codec, duration, width, height, target bitrate, original size, frame rate, and output filename. Example input is a path to a raw video file. Example output is a sentence stating a specific video is being converted specifying all the gathered formatting data.

title: Sqlite Data Import Pipeline
spec: The script handles the ingestion of a raw text data file into a local relational database. The `import(datafile)` logic must determine the file size of the input data file in bytes, count the total number of data rows to be imported, determine the installed version of the database engine binary, find the size of the target database file before the operation begins, calculate the size of the database file after the data is inserted, retrieve the current system date for logging, find the active user identifier executing the process, and measure the exact duration of the import operation. The script outputs a report detailing the data file size, row count, database engine version, initial database size, final database size, date, user identifier, and import duration. Example input is a path to a text file. Example output is a summary of the data insertion process with all gathered metrics.

title: Nginx Traffic Access Profiler
spec: The script parses a web server access log to generate a quick traffic overview. The `summarize(accesslog)` logic must count the total number of web requests, find the total number of unique visitor internet protocol addresses, determine the single most frequently requested uniform resource locator, extract the maximum response size sent in bytes, find the most common hypertext transfer protocol status code, determine the busiest hour of the day by request count, extract the most frequently seen web browser user agent string, find the total number of requests resulting in a server error, and retrieve the current date to timestamp the report. The script outputs a comprehensive sentence containing the total request count, unique visitor count, top resource locator, max response size, common status code, busiest hour, common user agent, error count, and current date. Example input is a path to a log file. Example output is a sentence detailing the aggregated access metrics.

title: Node Package Update Manager
spec: The script manages dependencies for a software project by checking for and applying updates. The `upgrade(project)` function must extract the project name from the configuration file, determine the current installed version of a specific core package, query the package registry for the latest available version of that package, find the total number of dependencies listed in the project, count the number of outdated dependencies, retrieve the software license type of the project, get the author name from the configuration, determine the total size of the local dependency installation folder, and calculate the number of days since the core package was last updated. The script outputs a report summarizing the upgrade status including the project name, current version, latest version, total dependencies, outdated count, license type, author, installation folder size, and days since last update. Example input is a path to a project directory. Example output is a sentence stating the project upgrade status with all details.

title: Cluster Node Eviction Script
spec: The script safely removes workloads from a distributed computing node before maintenance. The `evict(nodename)` logic needs to retrieve the current scheduling status of the node, count the total number of application pods running on the node, determine how many of those pods belong to system services, extract the internal internet protocol address of the node, find the operating system image running on the node, determine the maximum capacity of pods the node can handle, generate a timestamp for the start of the eviction process, find the name of the cluster administrator to notify, and calculate the total time taken to drain the workloads. The script prints a report confirming the node status, total pod count, system pod count, internal address, operating system, maximum pod capacity, eviction timestamp, administrator name, and total drain time. Example input is the name of a compute node. Example output is a sentence confirming eviction and logging all metrics.

title: Python Dependency Folder Inspector
spec: The script inspects an isolated language environment to report on its configuration and installed libraries. The `analyze(environment)` function must extract the specific version of the programming language interpreter, determine the absolute path to the environment root directory, find the total number of installed third party libraries, extract the current version of the package installer tool, determine the name of the library that consumes the most disk space, find the total disk space used by all libraries, check the system path for the environment binary folder, retrieve the creation date of the environment directory, and find the default character encoding of the interpreter. The script outputs a report summarizing the interpreter version, environment path, library count, installer version, largest library name, total library size, binary path, creation date, and character encoding. Example input is a path to an environment folder. Example output is a sentence reporting the folder properties and extracted facts.

title: Payload Encryption Automation Script
spec: The script secures a sensitive document by applying cryptographic protection before transmission. The `protect(document)` flow must generate a random thirty two character passphrase, determine the exact byte size of the original unencrypted document, extract the base filename of the document, determine the file type or mime type of the original document, find the user identifier of the person executing the script, retrieve the current system time for a timestamp, determine the total disk space available in the output directory, calculate the final byte size of the encrypted document, and generate a temporary decryption command string. The script outputs a sentence confirming the protection status including the passphrase, original byte size, filename, mime type, user identifier, timestamp, available space, final size, and decryption command. Example input is a path to a text document. Example output is a sentence stating the document was secured alongside its sizes and details.

title: Log File Anonymization Filter
spec: The script processes a system log file to redact sensitive personal information before sharing. The `anonymize(logfile)` process must find the original size of the input file, count the total number of internet protocol addresses that were redacted, determine the total number of email addresses that were replaced, generate a timestamp string indicating when the redaction occurred, calculate the final size of the sanitized output file, determine the installed version of the text processing utility used, find the total number of lines that were modified during the process, and measure the total execution time. The script prints a report listing the original size, address count, email count, timestamp, final size, utility version, modified line count, and execution time. Example input is a path to a log file. Example output is a summary sentence of the anonymization process including all extracted metrics.

title: Php Source Code Linter
spec: The script analyzes a directory of source code to find syntax errors and compliance issues. The `lint(sourcecode)` routine needs to count the total number of code files in the directory, find the total number of lines of code across all files, determine the version of the code interpreter installed on the system, extract the number of files containing syntax errors, find the total count of deprecated function calls, determine the name of the file with the most errors, retrieve the current memory limit set for the interpreter, calculate the total execution time of the linting process, and get the system username running the check. The script outputs a sentence summarizing the file count, lines of code, interpreter version, error file count, deprecated call count, worst file name, memory limit, execution time, and system username. Example input is a path to a source code directory. Example output is a sentence stating the validation results and all counted metrics.

title: In Memory Datastore Clearer
spec: The script performs a controlled clearing of an in memory data store instance. The `evict(instance)` logic must retrieve the specific version of the data store software, determine the total amount of memory currently used by the data store, find the total number of keys stored in the database, extract the system uptime of the data store service in seconds, determine the number of currently connected client applications, retrieve the configured maximum memory limit, get the network port the instance is listening on, measure the exact duration in milliseconds it takes to clear the keys, and find the hostname of the server. The script prints a report confirming the software version, memory used, key count, system uptime, client count, memory limit, network port, execution duration, and server hostname. Example input is a connection string or instance name. Example output is a sentence confirming keys were cleared returning all the gathered statistics.

title: System Startup Service Auditor
spec: The script analyzes the system boot sequence to report on background service initialization. The `audit(services)` entry must count the total number of background services enabled to start at boot, determine the name of the service that started the fastest, extract the name of the service that took the longest to initialize, calculate the total cumulative time taken for all services to start, find the exact timestamp when the operating system began booting, retrieve the active system kernel version string, determine the machine hardware architecture, and find the current system runlevel or target state. The script prints a report containing the enabled service count, fastest service, slowest service, total startup time, boot timestamp, kernel version, architecture, and runlevel. Example input is a service manager target. Example output is a summary of the boot performance metrics outputting all requested details.

title: Html Page Content Scraper
spec: The script downloads a web page and extracts key structural information for analysis. The `scrape(website)` logic needs to extract the main title text of the page, count the total number of hyperlinks present in the markup, determine the total number of image tags on the page, extract the meta description content string, calculate the total word count of the visible body text, find the primary domain name of the website, determine the total size of the downloaded page in kilobytes, retrieve the hypertext transfer protocol response time in milliseconds, and get the current date and time of the scrape. The script outputs a summary report detailing the page title, hyperlink count, image count, meta description, word count, domain name, page size, response time, and scrape date. Example input is a uniform resource locator string. Example output is a sentence stating a page was scraped bringing all extracted properties together.

title: Image Dataset Class Balancer
spec: Write a function `balance(dataset)` that accepts a dataset folder containing image files grouped into class subfolders. The logic must determine the total number of subfolders, the total number of images across all folders, the name of the subfolder with the most images, and the number of images in that largest subfolder. It should also find the name of the subfolder with the fewest images, the number of images in that smallest subfolder, the average number of images per subfolder, and the file size of the largest single image in the entire dataset. Return a list of these computed values. Example input: a folder containing animal categories. Example output: a list containing two, five hundred, dogs, three hundred, cats, two hundred, two hundred fifty, and four megabytes.

title: Codebase Complexity Metric Collector
spec: Write a function `evaluate(project)` that accepts a project folder path containing source code files. The logic must calculate the total number of text files, the total line count across all these files, the number of blank lines, and the number of lines containing comments. It must also determine the name of the file with the highest line count, the number of lines in that largest file, the name of the file with the longest single line, and the length of that longest line. Compute and return these metrics as a formatted sentence describing the project complexity. Example input: a web application folder. Example output: a sentence stating the project has ten files with two hundred total lines, twenty blank lines, thirty comment lines, where the main file contains fifty lines and the router file has the longest line of eighty characters.

title: Garbage Collection Log Analyzer
spec: Write a function `analyze(logfile)` that accepts the path to a plain text garbage collection log. The logic must extract the total number of garbage collection events, the timestamp of the first event, the timestamp of the last event, and the total duration of all pauses combined. It must also find the longest single pause duration, the line number where this maximum pause occurred, the shortest pause duration, and the average pause duration across all events. Return a list containing these extracted and computed data points. Example input: a text file with fifty log entries. Example output: a list with fifty, morning, noon, five seconds, one second, line twenty, one millisecond, and one hundred milliseconds.

title: Desktop Shortcut Icon Validator
spec: Write a function `validate(desktop)` that accepts a directory path containing desktop application shortcut files. The logic must determine the total number of shortcut files present, the number of files that are missing an execution path, and the number of files pointing to missing icon images. It must also find the name of the shortcut most recently modified, its modification date, the name of the oldest shortcut, its creation or modification date, and the total disk space consumed by the shortcut directory. Return a list of these validation metrics. Example input: a folder with user application launchers. Example output: a list containing twenty, zero, two, browser, yesterday, calculator, last year, and forty kilobytes.

title: Process File Descriptor Auditor
spec: Write a function `audit(pid)` that accepts a numeric process identifier. The logic must determine the current user running the process, the name of the executable, the total number of file descriptors currently opened by the process, and the maximum soft limit for open files allowed for this process. It must also find the maximum hard limit for open files, the path of the oldest accessed file descriptor, the path of the most recently accessed file descriptor, and the percentage of the soft limit currently consumed. Return a sentence summarizing these process details. Example input: a process identifier of a running web server. Example output: a sentence stating the web server run by the admin user has ten open files out of a soft limit of one thousand and hard limit of four thousand, with the oldest being the access log, the newest being a socket, consuming one percent of the limit.

title: Continuous Integration Build Summarizer
spec: Write a function `summarize(build)` that accepts the path to a continuous integration build output file. The logic must extract the build identification number, the name of the user or trigger that started the build, the exact start time, and the exact end time. It must also determine the total duration of the build, the final status outcome, the number of compilation warnings generated, and the number of failing tests reported. Return a list of these build summary points. Example input: a text file containing the output of a software compilation pipeline. Example output: a list with forty, webhook, morning, noon, four hours, success, zero, and zero.

title: Container Resource Quota Fetcher
spec: Write a function `fetch(container)` that accepts a path to a container control group directory. The logic must extract the configured memory limit in bytes, the current memory usage in bytes, the highest recorded memory usage, and the number of out of memory kill events. It must also determine the processor quota allocation, the processor period allocation, the total processor time consumed, and the current number of active tasks or processes running inside the control group. Return a list containing these resource metrics. Example input: a path to a system slice directory. Example output: a list with one gigabyte, fifty megabytes, sixty megabytes, zero, one hundred thousand, one hundred thousand, five seconds, and three.

title: Retail Sales Transaction Summarizer
spec: Write a function `process(transactions)` that accepts a path to a comma separated values file containing retail sales transactions. The logic must determine the total number of transactions, the sum of all transaction amounts, the highest single transaction amount, and the lowest single transaction amount. It must also find the average transaction amount, the total number of unique customer identifiers, the date of the earliest transaction, and the date of the latest transaction. Return a list of these financial metrics. Example input: a file with daily store sales. Example output: a list containing one hundred transactions, five thousand dollars, two hundred dollars, five dollars, fifty dollars, eighty customers, January first, and January thirty first.

title: Test Suite Result Aggregator
spec: Write a function `aggregate(results)` that accepts a path to a text file containing the output of a software test suite. The logic must extract the total number of tests executed, the number of tests that passed successfully, the number of tests that failed, and the number of tests that were skipped. It must also find the name of the test module that took the longest to run, its execution duration, the overall duration of the entire test suite, and the name of the operating system environment where the tests were executed. Return a list containing these extracted values. Example input: a file with automated test results. Example output: a list with fifty, forty, five, five, database tests, ten seconds, one minute, and linux.

title: Peripheral Device Power Analyzer
spec: Write a function `measure(bus)` that accepts a directory path representing a hardware peripheral bus system. The logic must determine the total number of connected peripheral devices, the number of devices currently active, the total power consumption requested by all devices combined, and the highest power consumption requested by a single device. It must also find the manufacturer name of the device using the most power, the product name of that device, the lowest power consumption requested by any active device, and the average power consumption across all devices. Return a formatted sentence describing these power metrics. Example input: a path to a peripheral bus virtual filesystem. Example output: a sentence stating ten devices are connected with five active, using five hundred milliamps total, averaging fifty, with the maximum being two hundred requested by the external drive from the storage vendor, and the minimum being ten.
